correctness.rationale: Explicit characteristic-five gradient equations prove smoothness if and only if t cubed differs from 3. The Čech construction and coefficient extraction from the fourth power of the defining sextic yield a ten-entry, ten-by-ten Hasse–Witt matrix and determinant t to the thirteenth power times (t cubed minus 1). A Frobenius-invariant decomposition into three diagonal lines, three invertible swap blocks, and one elliptic line proves the stable ranks 0, 9 and 10, separately from the one-step ranks. An independent symbolic multinomial/convolution calculation and an exhaustive 25-parameter finite-field check replay in the embedded verifier; the infinite-family conclusion follows from the displayed symbolic proof.

originality.rationale: A read of the exact motivating Badr–Bars family in the final open-access article reveals only automorphism stratification, explicitly restricted to characteristic zero or greater than 21, not the present characteristic-five rank classification. The inspected Borges–Gonçalves Fermat-type full text covers the Fermat case and other distinct families, not the nine-dimensional ordinary Prym complement or the three intermediate rank-nine parameters. Searches in mathematical literature and recorded earlier claims identified no implication covering this combined trichotomy. This is a best-knowledge claim subject to unindexed-priority risk.
residual_risks: Equivalent work in unindexed or inaccessible literature cannot be excluded.

value.rationale: A complete smooth-parameter stratification of two fundamental genus-ten Jacobian invariants for a natural published highly symmetric plane-sextic family. The nontrivial rank-nine locus, isolated superspecial Fermat member, generic ordinary family, and uniformly ordinary nine-dimensional complement are structurally meaningful, with a directly interpretable elliptic quotient and no reliance on a mere finite census.
